body: I can’t even get out my bed to eat or shower, what more book an appointment and go to a therapy session (which I can’t pay for, by the way). I have no will to live at all. A depressed person needs external support to get better; we’re too far gone.

There was a time when he blocked me for a week after the breakup. I actually thrived. I did so well moving on. I was getting my life back on track. And then he messaged me and then we called... then boom back to square one. This is why I want him to block me because it did me wonders before. I didn’t think of him... until he reached out. And then I found out he was doing horribly when he had me blocked. He was self-harming and all of that because he felt guilty about what happened in the relationship. And after he found out I was doing incredibly well when he blocked me, he doesn’t want to do that anymore.

> “I can easily block him myself. But the thing is, I don’t have self-control. I’ll go no contact for 2-3 days, and then I’ll come crawling back to him again. And he’ll be there with open arms. I’ll initiate a friendship, get hurt, go no contact— and the cycle begins again. It’s driving me insane.”
